questions.question: What is an important goal of intermediate sailing?
choices: Developing better control of the boat and sail
Avoiding all changes in sail trim
questions.explanation: Intermediate sailing focuses on developing better boat handling, sail control, and decision-making in changing conditions.

questions.question: When sailing faster, what should the sailor pay particular attention to?
choices: The shape of the rudder handle
questions.explanation: As boat speed increases, maintaining balance and proper sail trim becomes increasingly important.

questions.question: A sailor wants to improve boat speed without simply steering harder. What should the sailor examine first?
questions.explanation: Boat balance and sail trim have a major effect on how efficiently a dinghy moves through the water.

questions.question: What is a useful intermediate sailing habit?
choices: Make large control changes whenever possible
Observe the boat, wind, and sail and make small adjustments
Keep every control in the same position
questions.explanation: Good sailing involves observing conditions and making controlled adjustments rather than making unnecessary large changes.

questions.question: Why is boat balance important when sailing a dinghy?
choices: It helps the boat sail efficiently
It increases the weight of the boat
It prevents the wind from changing
questions.explanation: Keeping the boat balanced helps maintain efficient movement through the water and allows the sails to work effectively.

questions.question: If a dinghy begins to heel excessively to one side, what should the sailor normally do?
choices: Move to help balance the boat
Stand on the opposite side of the mast
Pull the tiller as hard as possible
questions.explanation: The sailor can use body position and sail controls to help restore the boat to a balanced attitude.

questions.question: What can happen when a dinghy is sailed with poor balance?
choices: The boat may become less efficient and harder to control
questions.explanation: Poor balance can increase drag, reduce efficiency, and make the boat more difficult to control.

questions.question: When the wind suddenly increases, why might the sailor need to adjust body position?
choices: To help keep the boat balanced
questions.explanation: A stronger wind can increase heeling force, so the sailor may need to change position to maintain balance.

questions.question: What primarily controls the boom angle on a dinghy?
questions.explanation: The mainsheet controls the boom and therefore controls the angle of the mainsail.

questions.question: When sailing closer to the wind, what generally happens to the boom angle?
choices: The boom is brought closer to the centerline
The boom is always released completely
The boom moves directly over the bow
The boom is removed from the boat
questions.explanation: When sailing closer to the wind, the mainsail is generally trimmed in, bringing the boom closer to the centerline.

questions.question: When bearing away from the wind, what should generally happen to the boom?
choices: It should be pulled completely to the center
It should remain fixed regardless of the wind
questions.explanation: As the boat bears away, the sail generally needs to be eased so the boom moves farther out.

questions.question: Why is correct boom angle important?
choices: It helps the sail produce useful aerodynamic force
It prevents the rudder from turning
questions.explanation: Correct boom angle helps position the sail appropriately relative to the wind.

questions.question: What does the outhaul primarily control?
choices: The tension along the foot of the mainsail
questions.explanation: The outhaul controls tension along the foot of the mainsail and influences the sail's shape.

questions.question: What generally happens to sail depth when the outhaul is tightened?
questions.explanation: Tightening the outhaul stretches the sail along its foot and generally flattens the lower part of the sail.

questions.question: Why might a sailor use a tighter outhaul in stronger wind?
choices: To stop the rudder from moving
questions.explanation: Flattening the sail can help reduce excessive power and make the boat more manageable in stronger wind.

questions.question: What is one reason to ease the outhaul?
choices: To allow a fuller sail shape
questions.explanation: Easing the outhaul allows more depth in the sail, which can be useful when additional power is desired.

questions.question: What does the vang primarily control?
choices: The downward position of the boom
questions.explanation: The vang controls downward tension on the boom and influences mainsail leech tension.

questions.question: Why can the vang be important when sailing downwind?
choices: It helps control the boom and sail shape
questions.explanation: When the mainsheet is eased substantially, the vang can help maintain control of the boom and sail shape.

questions.question: What generally happens when the vang is tightened?
choices: Downward tension on the boom increases
questions.explanation: Tightening the vang applies downward force to the boom and affects the shape and leech tension of the mainsail.

questions.question: Why should a sailor understand the relationship between vang and mainsheet?
choices: Both can affect mainsail shape and boom control
questions.explanation: The vang and mainsheet work together to control the boom and influence mainsail shape.

questions.question: What does the downhaul primarily control?
choices: Tension near the luff of the sail
questions.explanation: The downhaul controls tension along the luff of the sail and can significantly affect sail shape.

questions.question: What generally happens to the upper part of the sail when downhaul tension is increased?
choices: The sail becomes flatter and the leech can open
questions.explanation: Increasing downhaul tension can flatten the sail and open the upper leech, reducing power in stronger wind.

questions.question: Why might a sailor increase downhaul tension in stronger wind?
choices: To help depower and flatten the sail
To stop the boat from moving
questions.explanation: More downhaul tension can flatten the sail and help control excessive power in stronger wind.

questions.question: What is the main reason for adjusting the downhaul?
choices: To adjust mainsail shape for the conditions
To change the boat's hull length
questions.explanation: The downhaul is an important sail-control system used to adjust mainsail shape according to sailing conditions.

questions.question: Why is sailor position important in a dinghy?
choices: It affects boat balance and performance
questions.explanation: The sailor's position has a direct effect on the boat's balance, trim, and performance.

questions.question: When the boat heels too much to one side, what can the sailor do?
choices: Move their body to help balance the boat
questions.explanation: Moving body weight can help counteract heeling and maintain a more balanced boat.

questions.question: Why might a sailor move farther outboard in stronger wind?
choices: To use body weight to counteract heeling
questions.explanation: Moving outboard allows the sailor to use their body weight as leverage against the force of the wind.

questions.question: What is generally desirable when positioning yourself in a dinghy?
choices: Maintain a position that keeps the boat balanced and responsive
Always sit in exactly the same location
questions.explanation: Good sailor positioning keeps the boat balanced and allows the sailor to respond effectively to changes in wind and boat motion.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a daggerboard?
questions.explanation: The daggerboard provides lateral resistance and helps the boat make useful progress, especially when sailing upwind.

questions.question: What is generally appropriate for the daggerboard when sailing upwind?
choices: Keep it sufficiently down to provide lateral resistance
questions.explanation: A sufficiently lowered daggerboard provides the lateral resistance needed when sailing upwind.

questions.question: Why might a sailor raise the daggerboard when sailing in shallow water?
choices: To prevent it from hitting the bottom
questions.explanation: Raising the daggerboard in shallow water helps prevent damage from contact with the bottom.

questions.question: What may happen if too much daggerboard is used when sailing downwind?
questions.explanation: The daggerboard creates underwater resistance, so its position should be appropriate for the point of sail and conditions.

questions.question: Why should a sailor pay attention to changes in wind conditions?
choices: Wind changes affect boat handling and sail trim
Wind changes alter the hull color
Wind changes determine the water temperature
Wind changes make the daggerboard disappear
questions.explanation: Changes in wind speed and direction directly affect sail power, boat balance, and the controls needed.

questions.question: What should a sailor do when the wind suddenly becomes stronger?
choices: Adjust sail trim and boat balance as necessary
Always point directly into the wind
questions.explanation: A sudden increase in wind may require adjustments to sail controls and sailor position to maintain control.

questions.question: What is a wind shift?
questions.explanation: A wind shift occurs when the direction from which the wind is coming changes.

questions.question: If wind conditions become too strong for the sailor's experience or equipment, what is the safest choice?
choices: Reduce the risk by returning or postponing sailing
Increase speed as much as possible
questions.explanation: Sailing conditions should always be matched to the sailor's skill level and equipment. If conditions become unsuitable, reducing exposure to the risk is the safer decision.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of improving sailing performance?
choices: To make the boat move more efficiently
To eliminate the need for steering
To prevent the wind from changing
questions.explanation: Improving performance means using the wind, sails, boat, and sailor position more efficiently.

questions.question: Which combination is most important for good dinghy performance?
choices: Boat balance, sail trim, and sailor position
Hull color, sail number, and painter length
Water temperature, mast color, and rudder shape
Boat weight, beach location, and sail number
questions.explanation: Boat balance, sail trim, and sailor position work together to influence the boat's efficiency and speed.

questions.question: A sailor notices the boat is slow even though the wind is steady. What should the sailor check?
choices: Boat balance, sail trim, and control settings
The number painted on the sail
questions.explanation: When conditions are steady, checking balance and sail-control settings can help identify reasons for poor performance.

questions.question: What is a useful way to improve sailing performance over time?
choices: Observe the results of adjustments and practice consistently
Change every control at the same time
questions.explanation: Performance improves through observation, controlled adjustments, practice, and learning how the boat responds.
